question.text: Under FEMA and NDI Rules, foreign direct investment (FDI) is distinguished from foreign portfolio investment (FPI) by what threshold in a LISTED Indian investee company?

answer.text: FDI: ≥ 10% of post-investment fully diluted paid-up capital; FPI: < 10%
FDI and FPI are determined by investor type, not by percentage

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NDI Rules, FDI requires investment of ≥ 10% of post-investment fully diluted paid-up capital of the investee. FPI is < 10% in listed Indian investee. FPIs must register with SEBI under (FPI) Regulations 2019 before investing. The Trap: Option A (5%) confuses with Takeover Regulation 29. Option C (26%) is a strategic-foreign-investment threshold. Option D overstates the investor-type aspect. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C/D, X-A test FEMA routes. XIX-E cares for Cat III funds with offshore feeder routes.
